newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurocourt rules against Turkey on Cyprus case.
newsitem.headline: Eurocourt rules against Turkey on Cyprus case.

text.p: The European Court of Human Rights ruled on Wednesday that Turkey had violated the right to property of a Greek Cypriot woman who lost access to her land in northern Cyprus when Turkish troops invaded in 1974.

In a widely-watched case expected to set a precedent, the Court dismissed Turkey's argument that the European human rights convention did not apply to its occupation of the northern half of the Mediterranean island since it occurred before Ankara accepted its jurisdiction.
The Court ruled by 11 votes to six that Turkey nad violated Titina Loizidou's property rights by denying her access to plots of land in Kyrenia, northern Cyprus.
It gave Turkey six months to submit observations on Loizidou's claim for compensation.

But it dismissed her claim that she had lost her home, noting that she had not been living in Kyrenia at the time and that her intention to live in one of the flats she had been building in northern Cyprus "strained the meaning of the notion "home"."
